images.caption: Figure 1:WinARDet overview.Grounding Performance across Densities(Left):WinARDet outperforms the baseline across benchmarks of varying scene densities(Lin et al. (2014);Xia et al. (2018);Cheng et al. (2023);Goldman et al. (2019)), with increasingly pronounced gains in denser scenes.Breaking Box Repetition Loop(Middle):WinARDet breaks the box repetition loop, suppressing repeated predictions and recovering substantially more distinct objects.Beyond Bounding Boxes(Right):WinARDet generalizes to polygon detection, extending beyond bounding-box.

Figure 2:(a)Metrics are averaged over intervals of 100 predicted boxes on RSDense(Section4).
FHAR(left) rapidly accumulates redundant predictions as new-object discovery collapses, whereas WinAR(right) suppresses redundancy and sustains the discovery of new objects.(b)The onset of the box repetition loop coincides with historical-answer attention takeover and reduced system-token attention in FHAR(left), while WinAR(right) maintains a more stable attention allocation.

Figure 4:Overview of the proposed Compressed Window Auto-Regression.(a)A long answer is partitioned into consecutive windows and processed sequentially.
Preceding windows are compressed into memory and combined with the multimodal prefix to condition the current window, on which cross-entropy loss is applied.(b)Structure of the Window History Compressor.
